summary: This work demonstrates superconducting Dayem bridges integrated on the same chips as transmon qubits as on-chip thermometers, extracting local cryogenic temperature from critical current measurements via the Bardeen relation without requiring microwave control or qubit-specific protocols. The Pd/Ti bilayer bridges (with $T_c = 166$ mK) show excellent stability and agreement with qubit-based thermometry above 50 mK, with measured $T_2^{\mathrm{Ramsey}}$ correlating inversely with independently measured chip temperature over the 15–150 mK range.
motivation: Superconducting qubits are sensitive to local chip temperature, which often differs from cryostat mixing chamber measurements due to imperfect thermalization and stray heating, yet existing thermometry methods either impose substantial experimental overhead (qubit-based thermometry) or require dedicated device structures incompatible with qubit platforms.
method: Three Dayem bridges fabricated lithographically as narrow superconducting constrictions in a Pd/Ti bilayer were co-integrated with 16 transmon qubits on high-resistivity silicon; critical current was extracted from I–V sweeps using a superconducting series array amplifier (SSAA), and the Bardeen relation $I_c(T) = I_c(0)[1-(T/T_c)^2]^{3/2}$ was used to infer temperature with $T_c$ and $I_c(0)$ calibrated against an ADR-based reference.
result: DB thermometers demonstrated stability with $<1.5$ mK variations over 30 minutes at high sensitivity; measured $I_c$ tracked MXC temperature above 50 mK and matched effective temperatures from 2 qubits with readout fidelity $>75\%$ up to 120 mK; concurrent thermometer operation showed no significant crosstalk with qubit $T_2^{\mathrm{Ramsey}}$ (Mann-Whitney $p > 0.05$). Below 50 mK the response saturated, attributed to insufficient electron thermalization through 200 µm$^2$ cooling pads or measurement-induced heating.
